author: Chris Ogden
releaseNotes:
1.3.5 - Door code refresh no longer floods Z-Wave (#24). Up to 1.3.4 the app re-read every slot of every lock each night at midnight, starting a lock every 90 seconds, so on hubs with large locks the reads overlapped and Z-Wave timed out for hours. The refresh is now Off by default, also on hubs that update, and reads one lock at a time: the next lock starts when the current one reports its codes (not before 1 s per slot, at least 60 s, then 30 s to settle) or after its time budget (3 s per slot, 2 to 20 minutes). The app page has a new Door code refresh section: a Scheduled refresh setting (Off, Weekly on Tuesday or Daily, at a random time between 01:00 and 03:59 hub time, picked once per hub), a Refresh door codes now button for all locks or one chosen lock, and the progress of a running refresh. Clicking Done no longer starts a refresh. The old midnight schedule is removed when you click Done after updating, or the next time it fires (it then reads no lock). Door code writing, reconcile, code naming, the prefix and the minimum code position are unchanged.
1.3.4 - First release through Hubitat Package Manager. Hubs that installed the app by hand: use HPM Match Up (see the README), don't Install it again. The app page and log lines now show the app name with the version ("SignalBricks Integration 1.3.4"), the app has a description of what it does, the page warns when the code name prefix is empty, and explains that "Status: Not registered" is expected (the dispatcher drives the app through its endpoints; lock events reach SignalBricks through SignalBricks Telemetry). The "webhook: No SignalBricks ID" log line is now at trace level instead of debug. Door code writing, reconcile and code naming are unchanged; API responses still carry the bare version.
